E-001.insightSummary: Regulators need a consolidated way to track compliance casework across producers and submissions

E-002.rawExcerpt: See a complete view of an organisation
E-002.insightSummary: Regulators cannot quickly understand an organisation's status because information is spread across pages and sources

E-003.insightSummary: Regulators rely on manual year-on-year comparison to detect inconsistencies and risk signals

E-004.rawExcerpt: View the full history of submissions and changes
E-004.insightSummary: Regulators need an auditable history of original and resubmitted data but currently track changes manually

E-005.insightSummary: Regulators need longitudinal access to historic datasets that are currently downloaded and stored outside the system

E-006.rawExcerpt: Monitor fee payments and financial obligations
E-006.insightSummary: Regulators cross-reference finance data manually to understand whether obligations have been paid

E-007.insightSummary: Regulators manually check Companies House or other sources to confirm an organisation is legitimate

E-008.insightSummary: Regulators export raw data into master spreadsheets because they do not trust system data as a single source of truth

E-009.rawExcerpt: Identify risk and prioritise regulatory work
E-009.insightSummary: Regulators use dashboards or manual reporting to find high-risk cases and distribute workload

E-010.insightSummary: Regulators record decisions in spreadsheet comments or separate notes rather than a structured case record

E-011.insightSummary: Regulators analyse exports in spreadsheets or BI tools to identify unusual changes or reporting behaviour

E-012.rawExcerpt: Report on regulatory performance and scheme activity
E-012.insightSummary: Regulators compile manual reports from spreadsheets and extracts for oversight and policy reporting

E-013.rawExcerpt: Manage accreditation cases for reprocessors and exporters
E-013.insightSummary: Regulators track accreditation progress and assessor notes in spreadsheets or shared documents

E-014.rawExcerpt: See a complete view of a reprocessor or exporter
E-014.insightSummary: Regulators compile key organisation, site, status, and compliance data from multiple sources

E-015.rawExcerpt: Track accreditation status and renewal deadlines
E-015.insightSummary: Regulators maintain manual trackers for accreditation periods and renewal dates

E-016.insightSummary: Regulators export evidence data and analyse it in spreadsheets to assess reasonableness

E-017.rawExcerpt: Compare evidence issued against reported recycling activity
E-017.insightSummary: Regulators manually reconcile evidence records with submissions and evidence reports

E-018.insightSummary: Regulators keep inspection outcomes and follow-up actions in spreadsheets or local documents

E-019.insightSummary: Regulators use spreadsheets to track investigation steps, findings, and case status

E-020.rawExcerpt: Verify organisation legitimacy and site information
E-020.insightSummary: Regulators manually check company details, operator sites, and authorised persons against external records

E-021.insightSummary: Regulators manually check documentation and shipment data to confirm exports meet requirements

E-022.rawExcerpt: Access historical accreditation and evidence data
E-022.insightSummary: Regulators review archived spreadsheets and downloads to assess prior accreditation and evidence issues

E-023.rawExcerpt: Identify unusual evidence patterns or risk signals
E-023.insightSummary: Regulators use BI tools or spreadsheet analysis on exported data to detect anomalies

E-024.rawExcerpt: Produce regulatory reporting and oversight metrics
E-024.insightSummary: Regulators compile manual reports from multiple datasets for PRN/PERN oversight

E-025.rawExcerpt: Monitor waste movements across the system
E-025.insightSummary: Regulators export and analyse waste movement data in spreadsheets or BI tools

E-026.rawExcerpt: Investigate suspicious or incomplete waste records
E-026.insightSummary: Regulators use filters and manual checks on exported data to find missing or unusual records

E-027.rawExcerpt: See a complete view of a waste operator
E-027.insightSummary: Regulators combine organisation, permit, role, and history information from multiple systems

E-028.rawExcerpt: Track waste records across the full chain
E-028.insightSummary: Regulators manually link records from production through transport to final treatment or disposal

E-029.insightSummary: Regulators monitor submission lists in spreadsheets to find unsubmitted or incomplete records

E-030.rawExcerpt: Compare reported waste volumes over time
E-030.insightSummary: Regulators export historical data to spreadsheets or BI tools to analyse changes over time

E-031.insightSummary: Regulators track case steps and enforcement outcomes in spreadsheets or separate systems

E-032.insightSummary: Regulators manually check operator registrations, permits, and licences across external sources

E-033.insightSummary: Regulators analyse patterns such as unusual waste flows or frequent reporting issues to prioritise action

E-034.insightSummary: Regulators cross-check reported volumes against permit limits manually

E-035.insightSummary: Regulators store historic extracts outside the system to review previous movements and reporting behaviour

E-036.insightSummary: Regulators compile reports from multiple datasets and tools to report on waste flows and compliance

E-037.rawExcerpt: Need to know whether EPR applies and whether registration is required
E-037.insightSummary: Organisation representatives need early clarity on whether their organisation is in scope and what they must do next.

E-038.rawExcerpt: Need a clear and secure way to access client accounts while keeping client data separate
E-038.insightSummary: Consultants need delegated access patterns that let them support multiple clients without creating data separation risks.

E-039.rawExcerpt: Need to understand whether to register directly or through a compliance scheme
E-039.insightSummary: Direct producers need clarity on the correct route into the service and what role a compliance scheme plays.

E-040.rawExcerpt: Need to know what data to gather and prepare before registration
E-040.insightSummary: Producers want to know what information to assemble before starting registration so they can avoid delays and poor-quality submissions.

E-041.rawExcerpt: Need to manage producer obligations and service tasks on behalf of clients
E-041.insightSummary: Scheme operators need delegated ways of managing producer registrations and obligations without breaking role boundaries.

E-042.rawExcerpt: Need to upload packaging data, validate it, and understand any errors
E-042.insightSummary: Producers need reporting flows that make validation outcomes and correction actions understandable.

E-043.rawExcerpt: Need to understand what evidence is required to meet recycling obligations
E-043.insightSummary: Direct producers want clearer guidance on what evidence satisfies obligations and how to provide it.

E-044.rawExcerpt: Need confidence that PRN/PERN evidence and obligation calculations are accurate
E-044.insightSummary: Producers need visibility and trust in evidence status, obligation calculations, and the overall recycling target position.

E-045.rawExcerpt: Need to understand what disposal fees are due and how they are calculated
E-045.insightSummary: Producers need clear visibility of fee liability, fee history, and what remains outstanding.

E-046.rawExcerpt: Need consistent help, guidance, and clear distinction between guidance and announcements
E-046.insightSummary: Organisation representatives need support, guidance, and communications that are timely, trackable, and easy to distinguish from one another.

E-047.rawExcerpt: Need to trust fee calculations without relying on off-service spreadsheets and tools
E-047.insightSummary: Compliance schemes want to trust service-held calculations and avoid parallel spreadsheet work.

E-048.rawExcerpt: Need upload templates and validation to be simplified, unified, transparent, and informative
E-048.insightSummary: Compliance schemes need clearer upload templates and much better validation feedback for bulk submissions.

E-049.rawExcerpt: Need knowledgeable helpdesk support, faster issue resolution, and feedback loops that result in change
E-049.insightSummary: Schemes need responsive support and clearer service communications so they can keep members compliant.

E-050.rawExcerpt: Need a single login, portfolio view of clients, PRN approval visibility, and ability to act across multiple clients
E-050.insightSummary: Consultants need multi-client account management and visibility across obligations, approvals, and deadlines.

E-051.rawExcerpt: Guidance is inconsistent, CSV formats are inaccessible, uploads fail with unclear errors, and access models create bottlenecks
E-051.insightSummary: Consultants experience a mix of guidance inconsistency, technical friction, and restrictive access controls that slow down client support.

E-052.rawExcerpt: Need access to reporting and packaging data from the service, potentially through APIs or direct data products
E-052.insightSummary: Consumers of reporting need packaged, trusted access to service data for analysis, oversight, and downstream use.

E-053.rawExcerpt: Need to know dates and deadlines for registering and submission, and understand the full submission process
E-053.insightSummary: The hierarchy reinforces that direct producers need practical clarity on timelines and the end-to-end submission process.

E-054.rawExcerpt: Need to share responsibility with a compliance scheme, know which obligations are mine, and manage scheme relationships
E-054.insightSummary: Indirect producers need clear role boundaries and ways to manage how compliance schemes act on their behalf.

E-055.rawExcerpt: Need to know who in the supply chain is responsible for what and how to correctly label packaging items and categories
E-055.insightSummary: Producers need stronger clarity around categorisation, supply-chain responsibility, and the data they should submit.

E-056.sourceReference: Circular economy UR_2026-04-12_09-58-24.pdf; Circular economy UR_2026-04-12_09-58-51.pdf
E-056.rawExcerpt: I need one, consistent source of truth for the RAM and changes from modulation so I can apply it correctly and explain it internally.
E-056.insightSummary: Producers want one trusted source of truth for RAM guidance so they can apply requirements confidently and explain them internally.

E-057.rawExcerpt: I need to know what the true cost of the RAM will be, both in terms of the RAM tiers and wider implications for my organisation.
E-057.insightSummary: Producers need visibility of the full cost of RAM, not just headline fees, to budget and avoid shocks.

E-058.sourceReference: Circular economy UR_2026-04-12_09-58-24.pdf; Circular economy UR_2026-04-12_09-57-42.pdf
E-058.rawExcerpt: I need visibility and access around the supply chain of my product, so that I can gather the data required to complete the RAM assessment.
E-058.insightSummary: Producers need visibility of supply-chain data sources and access to upstream information so they can complete RAM assessments accurately.

E-059.rawExcerpt: I need to convert the RAM from government guidance into a practical process, so that I can apply it effectively for my organisation and communicate how it works to members.
E-059.insightSummary: Compliance schemes need to translate RAM guidance into practical processes they can use with members.

E-060.rawExcerpt: Helpdesk channel a lot of user queries and feedback on the RPD service. We need to better understand how they work and what reporting they can provide ongoing.
E-060.insightSummary: Helpdesk teams need visibility of support queries and feedback so they can resolve issues and inform service improvement.

E-061.rawExcerpt: Need will mainly be on reporting, for instance performance and update, projections and forecasting.
E-061.insightSummary: Legal and policy stakeholders need reliable reporting and projections from the service for oversight and decision-making.

E-062.rawExcerpt: Producers need to know what evidence is required as part of the RAM assessment, how much is enough?
E-062.insightSummary: Producers need clearer guidance on what evidence is required for RAM assessments and the threshold for sufficiency.

E-063.rawExcerpt: Distributors need good understanding of the legislation, despite not being obligated so they can inform their customers appropriately.
E-063.insightSummary: Distributors need enough understanding of RAM legislation to advise customers even when they are not directly obligated.

E-064.rawExcerpt: Blue and clear glass can both qualify for Green, while similar colour cues in plastic can block a Green rating.
E-064.insightSummary: Producers need material-specific clarity on how packaging attributes affect RAM ratings, because similar features can change outcomes differently across materials.

E-065.rawExcerpt: The most common cause of overpayment is misclassifying packaging as household when it should be non-household, or getting nation of sale wrong.
E-065.insightSummary: Producers need confidence in household or non-household classification and nation-of-sale data so they can avoid overpaying and report accurately.

E-066.rawExcerpt: Producers are confused about why they may need to pay both PRNs and new pEPR disposal fees, and what each one is for.
E-066.insightSummary: Producers need clearer explanations of how PRNs, pEPR disposal fees, and other charges fit together so the compliance model feels understandable and fair.

E-067.rawExcerpt: You should check your waste contractor is digitally compliant and verify that collections and receipts are correctly logged in the service.
E-067.insightSummary: Waste producers need to verify that contractors record collections and receipts correctly in digital waste tracking so they can maintain duty-of-care compliance.

E-068.rawExcerpt: If a business imports packaged goods into the UK and meets the thresholds, it becomes an obligated producer responsible for the packaging on those goods.
E-068.insightSummary: Importers need clearer guidance on when imported packaged goods make them obligated producers and what reporting duties follow.

E-069.sourceReference: Circular Economy Strategy delayed until 2026; Key Topics From the 2 September 2025 DEFRA Circular Economy Forum; Residual waste reduction Environment Act target delivery plan; inline_notebooklm_2026-04-12_policy_chat_02
E-069.rawExcerpt: The Circular Economy Growth Plan is delayed, while major reforms and statutory targets continue moving forward.
E-069.insightSummary: Policy and strategy users need a clearer view of how delayed plans, statutory targets, and scheme milestones fit together so they can make decisions in the right order.

E-070.sourceReference: Defra issues update on packaging waste export digital service; Extended Producer Responsibility for packaging: Notification of SI Amendment; Packaging data: what to collect for extended producer responsibility; inline_notebooklm_2026-04-12_policy_chat_02
E-070.rawExcerpt: Packaging waste export digital service delays require interim arrangements for PRN and PERN trading and continued evidence handling.
E-070.insightSummary: Compliance schemes need clear interim processes when digital services are delayed so they can keep evidence, export, and trading activity moving without introducing confusion or risk.

E-071.sourceReference: Extended Producer Responsibility for packaging: Notification of SI Amendment sent to the European Union and commitment to continued engagement
E-071.rawExcerpt: Strategic amendments introduce closed-loop offset rules and delegated operational responsibilities through a Producer Responsibility Organisation.
E-071.insightSummary: Producers need clearer explanations of offset eligibility, delegated scheme roles, and how these affect charges and operational responsibilities.

E-072.sourceReference: Digital waste tracking service policy paper: February 2026 updates; Introduction to mandatory digital waste tracking: summary of proposals; DEFRA / waste-tracking-service - GitHub; inline_notebooklm_2026-04-12_policy_chat_02
E-072.rawExcerpt: Digital waste tracking uses a phased rollout, API-led submission model, and a Receipt of Waste API with beta testing before mandatory compliance.
E-072.insightSummary: Waste site operators need a clear onboarding path for API-led digital waste tracking, including how and when to implement receipt-of-waste events before compliance becomes mandatory.

E-073.rawExcerpt: Phase 2 brings carriers, brokers, and dealers into mandatory digital waste tracking, including record creation and customer-facing references.
E-073.insightSummary: Waste carriers need a clear view of their phase-2 digital tracking duties, including what they must record during collection and transfer and how to provide traceable references to customers.

E-074.rawExcerpt: Delays to packaging waste export digital services and new accreditation rules create a need for clear interim arrangements for PRN and PERN operations.
E-074.insightSummary: Reprocessors and exporters need continuity when accreditation rules and evidence services change so they can keep PRN and PERN activity moving without jeopardising compliance.

E-075.rawExcerpt: Mandatory digital waste tracking requires a non-digital route for the small number of users who are legitimately digitally excluded.
E-075.insightSummary: Digitally excluded users need a clear non-digital route into mandatory waste tracking so they can remain compliant without being blocked by digital-only processes.

E-076.rawExcerpt: Producers describe dual-use packaging classification as especially difficult because item-by-item assessment creates heavy burden and fee risk.
E-076.insightSummary: Producers need a practical way to classify dual-use packaging so they can report correctly without disproportionate effort or avoidable fee risk.

E-077.rawExcerpt: Operators may act as transporters, controllers, or both depending on whether they only move waste or also decide its classification and destination.
E-077.insightSummary: Waste operators need help understanding whether they are acting as a transporter, controller, or both, because the new permitting model assigns different responsibilities and permit routes to each role.

E-078.rawExcerpt: Technical competence will be mandatory under the new permit regime, with modular requirements, nominated-person accountability, and refresher expectations.
E-078.insightSummary: Waste operators need a clear path to meeting technical competence requirements, including what training applies to their role, who can act as the nominated person, and when evidence must be provided.

E-079.rawExcerpt: Publishing permit numbers and validating permits through digital waste tracking is intended to help producers verify legitimate operators and meet duty-of-care obligations.
E-079.insightSummary: Waste producers need a simple way to check that the operator collecting or arranging their waste is legitimate, so they can hand over waste with confidence and meet duty-of-care obligations.

E-080.rawExcerpt: Smaller operators may face proportionately heavier transition burdens from permit fees, technical competence requirements, administration time, and updating permit identifiers on vehicles and branding.
E-080.insightSummary: Smaller waste operators need proportionate transition support so new permit, competence, and branding requirements do not create avoidable cost or disruption.

E-081.rawExcerpt: I need to accept and treat waste correctly so that I comply with waste regulations. Receivers must confirm waste matches the transfer note and permit before accepting it.
E-081.insightSummary: Receivers need to verify incoming waste against documentation and permit scope at the point of receipt so they can accept or refuse consignments lawfully.

E-082.sourceReference: DWT User Groups June 25.pptx#slide-4; WTPG-DWT Phase 1 – Anticipated waste receivers support queries (based on UR)-120426-122634.pdf#page-1-3
E-082.rawExcerpt: I need to have consistent regulations no matter the UK nation so that waste can be managed and moved consistently across the UK nations.
E-082.insightSummary: Receivers need cross-nation consistency in guidance and data expectations so cross-border waste movements can be handled without duplicated interpretation.

E-083.rawExcerpt: I need to understand changes in regulations so that I can update my product to comply with the changes. I need to enable my software to integrate with the waste tracking API.
E-083.insightSummary: Software developers need timely requirement changes and stable API integration support so waste-industry software can remain compliant as policy evolves.

E-084.rawExcerpt: I need to know what information I must provide (for example mandatory and optional) so that I provide complete records and have more confidence that I comply with waste regulations.
E-084.insightSummary: Carriers need clear mandatory-versus-optional data requirements at collection and handover so they can keep routes moving while producing complete records.

E-085.rawExcerpt: I need to report waste data without extra burden. I need to know what information I must provide and to be made aware of changes to tracking waste.
E-085.insightSummary: Brokers and dealers need clearer requirements and timely change communication so they can support clients without adding avoidable admin overhead.

E-086.sourceReference: DWT User Groups June 25.pptx#slide-24-25-47; WTPG-Frontline officers-120426-122323.pdf#page-2-7
E-086.rawExcerpt: I need to have reliable and timely data which shows the safe and proper movement of waste so that we can spot and respond to irregularities.
E-086.insightSummary: Frontline regulators need reliable and timely movement data to detect and respond to irregularities quickly during operational enforcement.

E-087.sourceReference: DWT User Groups June 25.pptx#slide-28-29; WTPG-Data analysts-120426-122111.pdf#page-1-6
E-087.rawExcerpt: I need to gather national waste statistics so that I can guide the development of future policies.
E-087.insightSummary: Data analysts need reliable national-level statistics from tracking data to support policy development and strategic planning.

E-088.sourceReference: DWT User Groups June 25.pptx#slide-32-33-48; WTPG-Policy advisors-120426-122041.pdf#page-1-5
E-088.rawExcerpt: I need consistent high quality reliable data so that I can make policy decisions.
E-088.insightSummary: Policy makers need consistent and trustworthy tracking data to evaluate policy options and defend evidence-based decisions.

E-089.rawExcerpt: Data analysts expected both aggregated outputs and access to raw transactional data, with QA checks needed before data was useful.
E-089.insightSummary: Data analysts need both aggregated views and raw tracking data so they can validate quality issues, interrogate anomalies, and build the right outputs for different users.

E-090.rawExcerpt: Policy advisors repeatedly emphasised the importance of seeing where waste has come from and where it has gone, and wanted direct access when analysis became complex.
E-090.insightSummary: Policy advisors need trustworthy waste-flow data and direct access to interrogate it when necessary so they can support strategy, evaluate policy impact, and guide operational priorities.

E-091.rawExcerpt: Frontline officers often need permit-aligned site data, but specialist and senior roles also need flexible access across waste types, regions, and suspected misdescription.
E-091.insightSummary: Frontline officers need flexible access to permit, movement, and classification data so they can investigate irregularities ranging from simple site checks to complex hazardous waste cases.

E-092.sourceReference: WTPG-DWT Phase 1 – Anticipated waste receivers support queries (based on UR)-120426-122634.pdf#page-1-3
E-092.rawExcerpt: Waste receivers raised detailed questions about spreadsheet structure, data fields, terminology, validation, replacement scope, and transition to API submission.
E-092.insightSummary: Waste receivers need clear spreadsheet guidance, validation feedback, and explanation of what DWT replaces so they can submit Phase 1 data confidently even in manual or low-software environments.

E-093.rawExcerpt: Controllers prioritised the need to initiate transfers, know required fields, handle multiple EWC codes, manage repeat collections, review season tickets, and reclassify waste without restarting.
E-093.insightSummary: Waste controllers need practical workflows for repeat collections, multiple EWC codes, and reclassification so they can keep waste moving without recreating records from scratch.

E-094.rawExcerpt: Small producers repeatedly called out the need to know early whether pEPR now applies to them, whether their status has changed, and what obligations and fees that change creates.
E-094.insightSummary: Small producers need early clarity on whether they are now obligated under pEPR, what has changed, and what fees and preparation that creates for the business.

E-095.rawExcerpt: Small producers wanted to anticipate the data and time needed for account creation and compliance scheme selection, and some needed those tasks to be delegated to the colleague who actually understands the packaging data.
E-095.insightSummary: Small producers need the early pEPR onboarding journeys to be scoped clearly so the right person can complete them without unnecessary preparation or blocked delegation.
E-095.serviceStage: Account creation and compliance scheme declaration

E-096.sourceReference: Circular economy UR_2026-04-12_11-51-26.pdf#page-1; Circular economy UR_2026-04-12_11-51-34.pdf#page-1
E-096.rawExcerpt: The research findings describe carriers with low digital skills, weak connectivity, outdated or costly software, heavy training overhead, and strong dependence on paper and Excel workflows.
E-096.insightSummary: Carriers need a digital waste tracking route that works for low-margin, low-digital operations where connectivity, software fit, and training capacity are all real constraints.

E-097.sourceReference: Circular economy UR_2026-04-12_11-51-26.pdf#page-1; Circular economy UR_2026-04-12_11-51-34.pdf#page-1
E-097.rawExcerpt: Operators described frequent divergence between what is planned and what actually happens: misdescribed waste, mixed loads, receiver changes, weight corrections, contaminated skips, missing paperwork, and repeat visits.
E-097.insightSummary: Carriers need to update movements when collections change in the real world, without having to restart paperwork or lose traceability when waste differs from plan.

E-098.sourceReference: Circular economy UR_2026-04-12_11-51-26.pdf#page-1; Circular economy UR_2026-04-12_11-51-34.pdf#page-1
E-098.rawExcerpt: The boards repeatedly say producers often do not know what they are consigning, lack classification knowledge, and fail to provide WTNs or enough information, leaving handlers to police compliance.
E-098.insightSummary: Waste producers need clearer support to describe and hand over waste correctly, because classification and duty-of-care failures upstream create downstream delays, rework, and compliance risk.

E-099.rawExcerpt: Cannot download RPD registrations in Excel
E-099.insightSummary: Regulators need self-serve registration exports because current workflows rely on manual checking or separately supplied reports.

E-100.rawExcerpt: CS resubmissions not shown in RPD workflows
E-100.insightSummary: Regulators struggle to follow resubmitted scheme data because workflows do not clearly surface pending or revised submissions.

E-101.rawExcerpt: Regulators can't see the producer view of the service for specific issues
E-101.insightSummary: Support teams cannot diagnose producer problems quickly because they cannot access the same front-end view and journey context seen by producers.

E-102.rawExcerpt: Multiple compliance schemes can submit data for the same producer without validation
E-102.insightSummary: Regulators face duplicate and conflicting data risks because the service does not prevent multiple schemes from submitting for the same producer.

E-103.rawExcerpt: Approved person role and legal responsibility are unclear, and RPD does not support multiple approved persons
E-103.insightSummary: Registration support is slowed because approved-person responsibilities, legal accountability, and approval arrangements are not surfaced clearly in the service.

E-104.rawExcerpt: If user provide new email in registration file, it is not picked up by the RPD service
E-104.insightSummary: Regulators lose time chasing organisations because submitted contact changes are not reliably reflected in service records or easy to verify.

E-105.insightSummary: Compliance reporting is not trusted because report logic is too simplistic, does not match real compliance criteria, and does not keep up with regulatory change.

E-106.rawExcerpt: Direct producers need manual help to complete the process successfully, and uploads do not show pending state quickly enough
E-106.insightSummary: Manual support remains high because direct producers do not get clear confirmation when uploads are received or progressing, so regulators have to chase and reassure them.

E-107.rawExcerpt: User researcher contrasted UK throwaway culture with Denmark, where bottle-return machines, take-and-leave schemes, and pride in reused goods make reuse feel normal and socially valued.
E-107.insightSummary: Circular-economy outcomes depend on culture, incentives, and service presentation, not only regulatory reporting obligations.

E-108.rawExcerpt: Organisations do not think of themselves as producers; they describe themselves as businesses, manufacturers, cosmetics companies, OTC medication sellers, or supplement businesses.
E-108.insightSummary: Using policy language such as producer may fail to match how obligated organisations understand themselves and their role.

E-109.rawExcerpt: Experienced compliance users said they had never worked on a policy or scheme this hard to comply with, despite having worked on PPT and similar obligations elsewhere.
E-109.insightSummary: EPR complexity may work against the government's growth and red-tape reduction agenda by increasing compliance burden for businesses.

E-110.rawExcerpt: One organisation reduced paper packaging but found the smaller 40 by 40mm item was classified as red, increasing EPR cost despite lower material use.
E-110.insightSummary: Some EPR rules can unintentionally penalise packaging reduction, discouraging organisations from lower-material packaging choices.

E-111.rawExcerpt: User researcher described organisations moving from glass to plastic because PRN cost is weight-based and glass creates a higher bill, even where plastic may have worse environmental impacts.
E-111.insightSummary: Weight-based charging can create incentives to move away from heavier recyclable materials toward lighter fossil-fuel-based packaging.

E-112.rawExcerpt: A packaging-event example described a business considering home-compostable paper cups but refraining because residue such as hot chocolate could classify the packaging as red.
E-112.insightSummary: Compostable or reusable packaging innovation may be blocked where contamination or classification rules make the greener option financially unattractive.

E-113.rawExcerpt: User researcher hypothesised that organisations should be understood by submission complexity and supply-chain depth, because large or small producer status is too blunt to explain compliance burden.
E-113.insightSummary: Organisation size is a weak proxy for EPR complexity; packaging variety, supply-chain depth, and operating model may better explain burden and support needs.

E-114.rawExcerpt: A small organisation with about 50 people and GBP18m turnover employed a legally trained compliance officer who spends around 80% of her time on EPR; once they cracked submission, they were unlikely to change it because change is too costly.
E-114.insightSummary: The cost of understanding and maintaining EPR submissions can lock organisations into current packaging and data practices, reducing space for innovation.

E-115.rawExcerpt: User researcher argued the service needs data for three levels: policy evaluation, accountability for public spending and policy performance, and fair charging of organisations.
E-115.insightSummary: Data collection should be designed around explicit policy, accountability, and charging questions rather than collecting every possible field by default.

E-116.rawExcerpt: Organisations are experiencing change fatigue from unstable rules and multiple communications, and some are postponing investment in packaging-data software while waiting for EPR and EU PPWR requirements to stabilise.
E-116.insightSummary: Regulatory instability can delay investment in better data systems, increasing manual work and slowing readiness for UK and EU obligations.

E-117.rawExcerpt: User researcher described a ripple effect: unclear obligations lead to interpretation, paid advice, training burden, poor data quality, inaccurate charges, under-reporting, over-reporting, and false PRN demand that can distort prices.
E-117.insightSummary: Ambiguity in obligations has system-level consequences beyond individual support demand, including poorer data, unfair charging, and market distortion.

E-118.rawExcerpt: Industry feedback argues that pEPR fees charged in GBP per tonne create a financial misfire for heavier materials such as glass and metal, even where those materials may be more sustainably managed or recycled at higher rates than plastic.
E-118.insightSummary: Weight-based pEPR charging can disproportionately burden heavier packaging materials and may incentivise producers or retailers to move toward lighter plastic to manage costs.

E-119.rawExcerpt: Desk research distinguishes the volume-based costs local authorities incur when collecting and managing waste from the weight-based denominator used to bill producers by packaging category.
E-119.insightSummary: There is a contested gap between how waste-management costs are driven in practice and how pEPR charges are apportioned back to producers.

E-120.rawExcerpt: The government assessed industry feedback and confirmed in March 2025 that it was not considering unit-based fees, maintaining GBP per tonne as the correct apportionment under the 2024 regulations.
E-120.insightSummary: The government position is to retain weight-based fee apportionment while arguing that the model accounts for on-the-ground volume realities before final billing.

E-121.rawExcerpt: Rather than moving to unit-based fees, the government is encouraging glass producers to reduce pEPR liability through reuse and refill, with a planned autumn 2026 call for evidence on further reuse incentives.
E-121.insightSummary: Reuse and refill are positioned as the policy route for reducing recurring pEPR liability for heavier materials, but producers need clarity on how to make that transition commercially and operationally viable.
